summary.text: Lateefah Simon is the Democratic incumbent representing California's 12th Congressional District in the East Bay, which she has held since January 2025. She began as a youth-justice advocate in her teens and later led civil-rights and philanthropic organizations, served on the BART Board of Directors from 2016 to 2024, and was elected to Congress in 2024. She is running for re-election.

paragraphs.text: Simon was born in San Francisco in 1977. She earned a bachelor's degree in public policy from Mills College in 2009 and a Master of Public Administration from the University of San Francisco in 2022.

According to her official biography, her career began in her late teens at the Young Women's Freedom Center, where she became executive director at 19 and worked with young women and girls in the criminal justice and foster care systems.
She later led the Back on Track program, an alternative-to-incarceration initiative for first-time nonviolent offenders, in partnership with then-San Francisco District Attorney Kamala Harris.

Simon went on to serve as executive director of the Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights of the San Francisco Bay Area, program director at the Rosenberg Foundation, and president of the Akonadi Foundation and the Meadow Fund, according to her official biography.
Then-Gov. Jerry Brown appointed her to the Board of Trustees of the California State University in 2016, and Gov. Gavin Newsom appointed her in 2020 as a senior advisor on police reform.

Simon was elected to the Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) Board of Directors in 2016 and served through 2024, including as board president from 2020 to 2024; her office says she launched BART's Ambassador Program.
She won the U.S. House seat previously held by Barbara Lee in November 2024, defeating fellow Democrat Jennifer Tran in the general election, and Ballotpedia lists her tenure as beginning in 2025.

In the 119th Congress she serves on the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee and the Small Business Committee, and her office says she is a Deputy Whip for Policy and a Vice Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.

Her office lists recognitions including a MacArthur Fellowship, the John F. Kennedy Frontier Leadership Award and the Jefferson Award for Public Service, and she states that she is the mother of two daughters.
